config.title: RTK Query — Data Fetching & Cache

intro.title: RTK Query — Data Fetching & Cache
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple React application that fetches and displays a list of posts from a mock API. You'll learn how to use RTK Query, a powerful data fetching and caching tool from Redux Toolkit, to manage server state efficiently. The core concepts include creating an API service with endpoints, automatically handling loading and error states, and leveraging built-in caching to avoid unnecessary network requests. By the end, you'll have a functional app that demonstrates how RTK Query simplifies data fetching in React with TypeScript.
intro.usecase: RTK Query's data fetching and caching patterns are essential in modern web applications like e-commerce dashboards and social media feeds. In product dashboards, RTK Query efficiently manages real-time inventory updates and customer analytics while preventing duplicate API calls. Social media platforms use its automatic caching to instantly display previously loaded posts and comments when users navigate between pages.

objectives: Configure an RTK Query API service with endpoints for fetching and caching data
Integrate the RTK Query provider into your React application's store setup
Implement data fetching hooks in components to retrieve server data
Manipulate cached data by configuring refetching and polling behaviors
Control loading and error states using the status flags provided by RTK Query
Construct mutation endpoints to send data updates to the server
Apply cache tag invalidation to synchronize data after mutations

steps.title: Define baseQuery and empty endpoints
steps.instruction: Define it with a baseQuery using fetchBaseQuery and an empty endpoints object for now. The endpoints function receives a special object called builder — think of it as RTK's endpoint factory. You are giving it an empty toolbox here. In the next steps you will use builder.query(...) to register your first endpoint inside it.
steps.hint: Pass an object to createApi with baseQuery: fetchBaseQuery({ baseUrl: '...' }) and endpoints: (builder) => ({}). The builder parameter is RTK Query's way of letting you register typed endpoints — you will use it in the next step.
steps.expectedOutcome: The API service has baseQuery using fetchBaseQuery and an empty endpoints function.
successCriteria: The code includes baseQuery using fetchBaseQuery and an empty endpoints function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Now let's learn what goes inside that endpoints object before you write it.
steps.feedbackWrong: Define baseQuery with fetchBaseQuery and an empty endpoints object.

steps.title: Add getPosts query endpoint (no generics yet)
steps.instruction: Inside the endpoints object, add a getPosts entry using builder.query with a query function that returns '/posts'. Skip the TypeScript generics for now — just get the shape right first.
steps.hint:
Inside endpoints: (builder) => ({ ... }), add:
  getPosts: builder.query({ query: () => '/posts' })

Remember: RTK will combine your baseUrl ('https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com') with this path ('/posts') to make the full request URL.
steps.expectedOutcome: The endpoints object contains a getPosts entry using builder.query with a query function returning '/posts'.
successCriteria: getPosts is defined inside endpoints using builder.query with query: () => '/posts'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Solid! One more step — let's add the TypeScript types so RTK knows exactly what this endpoint returns.
steps.feedbackPartial: Add getPosts: builder.query({ query: () => '/posts' }) inside the endpoints object.
steps.feedbackWrong: Inside the endpoints arrow function, add: getPosts: builder.query({ query: () => '/posts' })

steps.title: Type the endpoint with TypeScript generics
steps.instruction: Now add TypeScript generics to builder.query so RTK knows the response type and argument type. Change builder.query to builder.query<Post[], void>. Post[] means the response is an array of Post objects. void means the hook takes no argument.
steps.hint: Change builder.query({ ... }) to builder.query<Post[], void>({ ... }). The two generics go between < and > right after builder.query — before the parentheses.
steps.expectedOutcome: The getPosts endpoint is fully typed with builder.query<Post[], void>.
successCriteria: builder.query is typed with <Post[], void> generics.
steps.feedbackCorrect: The API service is fully defined. Now let's wire it into the Redux store.
steps.feedbackPartial: Add <Post[], void> immediately after builder.query, before the opening parenthesis.
